doc.title: The 64 placed screws IN SITU, four regions, each render read back by the instrument that refused the whole-machine one

a_misreading_recorded: The first hip-left render was read as '20 coarse boxes, no real geometry' — i.e. as a broken render. That reading was WRONG and a two-part control settled it: the hip bracket draws as a real curved bracket with its bores, and the XL330 servo genuinely IS a rectangular box with a round output horn on one face. The boxes were correct parts. What the picture did show was a defect in THIS tool, not in the kernel: all 15 servo instances were drawn in all four regions because every region names the mesh. Hence the proximity filter above.
why: cecad.render.verify_render REFUSED the all-64-screws render and was right to: a cloud of 4 mm objects in a 300 mm frame has no continuous mark over 10 % of the frame. The answer is not to disable the check but to frame the picture a reader needs — screws beside the parts they fasten, at a scale where both are legible.
a_limitation_found_by_looking_at_the_hea: The head picture shows the head shell floating above a cluster of NINE servo boxes, and the head does not have nine servos. The servos are assigned to a region by nearest anchor part, and the head region's anchor list includes `neck`, which sits low on the machine — so trunk and hip servos fall closer to it than to their own region's anchors. This is a defect in the DISPLAY GROUPING only: every servo's world placement is the assembly's own, unchanged, and each appears exactly once across the four pictures (3 + 2 + 9 + 1 = 15). It is recorded rather than tuned away, because sweeping the grouping until the head shows three servos would be fitting the instrument to the expected answer. WHAT SETTLES IT: assign each servo to the region of the JOINT it actuates, read from ce-assemblies/microduck/current/joints.json, instead of by distance.
